A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Sudoku experiments in Table 2 and Figures 3–6, frontier-model evaluations in Appendix B, and 1-in-3 SAT results in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Sudoku evaluations and the 99.10% accuracy reported for 1-in-3 SAT in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The DFS procedure, action-level tokens, multi-target losses, depth-1 restart optimization, and Appendix D scratchpad remain unchanged. The added verification and successful-trajectory passages clarify the existing setup without establishing a changed algorithm or training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Random, Kaggle filtered/unfiltered, and RRN Sudoku data, plus generated 1-in-3 SAT instances. Appendix B retains the same three Sudoku input formats.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains RRN, Recurrent Transformer, Causal Transformer, and MDM comparisons; the frontier-model and oracle comparisons also remain unchanged. Figure 1 redisplays the two already evaluated proposed variants rather than introducing a new comparator.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, sample sizes, model configuration, and Appendix C training settings are unchanged. The successful-trajectory restriction is newly explicit documentation, not a reported revision to the experiments.

E4.justification: The tokenization/multi-target ablation, cross-dataset training curves, loss/oracle comparison, and input-format analyses are retained. No new ablation tests the added explanation about excluding unsuccessful trajectories.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point estimates and checklist justification based on large evaluation samples. There are no additions or revisions to repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8, the training and guessing curves, and Appendix G results are unchanged. Figure 1 now displays 98.9% and 99.8%, already reported in v1 Table 2 and Section 4; its previous 99% label rounded the imitation-learning result.

T1.justification: The loss definitions, assumptions, counterexample, contextual formulation, and approximation theorem and proof in Appendix E are unchanged. The new verifier discussion adds no formal mathematical result.

C1.justification: The core claims about trial-and-error reasoning, near-perfect Sudoku/SAT accuracy, guessing optimization, and puzzle generation are retained. The abstract newly highlights verification and depth-1 solvability, both already discussed in v1.

C2.justification: Sections 2 and 4 add an explanation attributing the depth-1 approach's advantage to training only on successful trajectories, arguing that imitation of failed paths encourages incorrect continuations. The existing depth-1 and non-adaptivity limitations remain intact.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents successful-only trajectories for beyond-imitation training and makes correctness verification more explicit. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, generator interfaces, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive relationships to prior Sudoku solvers, language models, and Min-Sum Set Cover research are unchanged. The bibliography is reflowed without changes to its content.

P1.justification: v2 expands the abstract and selected methodology paragraphs, adds the successful-trajectory explanation, and merges Summary with Limitations and future work into Section 5. Most prose and all substantive appendix content remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is widened and replaces the single Ours bar with separately labeled Imitation Learning and Beyond Imitation bars showing existing results. Other figures and tables retain their content, with limited text and reference reflow.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 makes successful-trajectory training and verification more explicit, while Figure 1 more clearly distinguishes the two proposed variants. These changes modestly improve clarity and reproducibility. The added causal explanation has no new isolating ablation, and the empirical and theoretical evidence remains unchanged, limiting the overall gain.
